newsitem.title: USA: Georgia militiamen get prison terms for bombs.
newsitem.headline: Georgia militiamen get prison terms for bombs.

text.p: Three Georgia militia members were sentenced by a federal judge on Thursday to several years in prison for their roles in a pipe-bomb conspiracy against the government.
Bob Starr III was given an 8-year, 1-month prison term for conspiring to use and possessing pipe bombs. Jimmy McCranie Jr. and Troy Spain were each sentenced to 6-1/2 years in prison.
The three men, members of the 112th Georgia Militia, were convicted on November 7 in a trial that lasted almost a month.

During a two-day sentencing hearing held under tight security, Assistant U.S. Attorney Sam Wilson said the men had built five pipe bombs and had buried enough material on Starr's property to make at least 14 more. An informant recorded McCranie saying he'd like to build as many as 100 bombs.

"The Congress has sent a message out that if you have pipe bombs, you're going to jail for a long time," Wilson told reporters after the sentences were handed down by U.S. District Judge Duross Fitzpatrick.

Starr told the judge he "had no intentions of hurting anyone" and said had been set up by government informants. Defence attorneys said all three men would appeal their sentences on the basis of entrapment.
Tapes made by government informants indicated the men were preparing for a government crackdown on militia groups and gun owners that would have involved the use of United Nations troops.
